method: Lines sampled across every scene (dad call, door confrontation, table scene with the fake travel-agent call, street, sneaking out, café, kitchen, bedroom, farewell, balcony, café cliffhanger). For each line 4 frames evenly spaced over the line (runs/gt/fjGrX8aBVAc/frames_spk/f_*.jpg) were checked for who is on screen and whose mouth moves, combined with content (names used, who answers whom). Speaker decided before looking at Scribe labels; Scribe label (majority word speaker by time overlap) added afterwards.

label_conventions.speaker: character name from the list; 'OFFSCREEN:<name>' = the speaker is not visible during the line (phone voice, reaction shot held on a listener) but is identified from content/voice context; 'UNKNOWN' = cannot tell. For diarization scoring, strip the OFFSCREEN: prefix.
label_conventions.confidence: 3 = seen speaking and/or unambiguous from content; 2 = likely (wide shot or cut mid-line, content supports); 1 = guess
label_conventions.times: seconds in the episode audio; keyed by time, not by Scribe line id
label_conventions.on_screen: everyone visible at any moment during the line (union over frames sampled inside the line's start-end; a cut that lands just outside the line does not count); [] = nobody (an insert shot such as a sign or a phone screen); on_screen_partly = only a back of the head / shoulder / hand / blurred edge is visible (over-the-shoulder foregrounds, a sleeve at the frame edge), not identifiable as a face; a whole figure seen from behind counts as on_screen. Background extras who never speak are not listed; known characters are listed even when silent or small in the background. Independent of speaker: the speaker may be off screen while others are shown. on_screen_note = what was seen, when useful.
label_conventions.voices: only on lines with more than one voice: a list in time order of {from_text: the first word of that voice's part, copied from the line's text, speakers: [names]}; two people one after another = two entries; several people saying it together (group line, everyone laughing a word) = one entry with several names. Lines without voices were checked and have a single voice (clip-gt-editor 2026-11-02: Scribe word speakers inside the line, content, frames; no line in this key needed it).

hard_cases: Scribe gives both women one label; every Meera/Harshita line here was decided from frames (costume per scene, mouth movement) and from content (Meera calls him Vijay, Harshita calls him Abhi).

5:29-6:53 is cross-talk: Meera on the phone with the friend (fake travel agent) while Harshita and Abhi argue in whispers; lines were assigned by which shot the line plays over plus content (travel offer = friend/Meera, 'Vijay'/'cafe'/'పేరు మార్చుకోవడం' = Harshita).
5:42 'ఏంటి మీరా దగ్గర ఇరికించున్నావ్?' is played on Abhi with his mouth moving; read as Abhi accusing Harshita (confidence 2).
8:34 'సినిమాకి' (the lie) vs 'Cafe కి వెళ్తున్నాం' (the truth): two-shot, assigned Abhi then Meera by content and mouth.
10:22 'సింధు' and 11:30 'Onions ఇవ్వా' could not be attributed (UNKNOWN).
Asides spoken with lips closed (Harshita 3:30, 10:12; Abhi 4:15) are labelled as the thinking character.
